title: Solve it: a mixed find-and-keep round
idea: GUIDED PROBLEM (review round). Interleaves filter, search, and earlier list tools (sum, max, len) across a couple of small tasks, so the learner picks the right tool each time. Review-heavy, as the last lesson of the unit.
problem: Donations today were [20, 5, 50, 5, 35]. Three small tasks: (A) keep the donations of 20 or more; (B) was there a donation of exactly 50? (C) what was the largest donation?

exercises.prompt: Three tasks on donations = [20, 5, 50, 5, 35]. Match each task to the kind of OUTPUT it needs. Task A: 'keep donations of 20 or more.'
exercises.explanation: 'Keep the ones that match' collects items into a new list — a filter.

exercises.prompt: Task B: 'was there a donation of exactly 50?' What output?
exercises.explanation: 'Was there...?' is a presence question — a search giving True/False.

exercises.prompt: Task C: 'what was the largest donation?' Which earlier pattern fits?
options: track-the-best: start at the first, keep the larger while looping
exercises.explanation: The biggest value comes from the track-the-best pattern (Unit 59): start biggest at the first item, then keep the larger one as you loop.

exercises.prompt: Example, Task A. By hand, keep 20-or-more from [20, 5, 50, 5, 35]. Which stay?
exercises.explanation: 20 (exactly), 50, and 35 qualify; the two 5s do not. Kept list is [20, 50, 35].

exercises.prompt: Examples, Tasks B and C. By hand: is 50 present, and what is the max?
exercises.explanation: 50 appears, so True; the largest value is 50. Your check values: True and 50.

exercises.prompt: Code Task A (filter). Arrange the lines.
exercises.explanation: Store donations and the limit, start big_gifts empty, keep each gift >= limit, then print the list.

exercises.prompt:
Code Task B (search). Complete it:

donations = [20, 5, 50, 5, 35]
wanted = 50
found = wanted ____ donations
print(found)
exercises.explanation: 'in' asks whether 50 is present and gives True/False — the whole search in one line.

exercises.prompt: Code Task C (largest). Arrange the lines to find the biggest donation with a loop.
exercises.explanation: Start biggest at the first donation, then walk the list and keep the larger value whenever you find one. That is the track-the-best pattern from Unit 59.

exercises.prompt: Check. The code prints [20, 50, 35], then True, then 50. Your hand examples were [20, 50, 35], True, 50. Verdict?
exercises.explanation: Every output matches its by-hand example, so filter, search, and max each solved their task correctly.

exercises.prompt: New day, same three plans: donations = [10, 60, 10]. What do A (limit 20), B (wanted 50), and C print?
exercises.explanation: A keeps only 60 (>= 20); B finds no 50, so False; C's max is 60. Each tool generalizes to the new inputs — you've practiced find-and-keep end to end!
